chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Uqba, from Sayaaba ibn Ayyoub and Muhammad ibn al-Walid and Ali ibn Asbaat, they raise it to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah will punish six (groups) for six (sins): the Arabs for tribal prejudice (al-'asabiyyah), the landlords (al-dahaqeen) for arrogance (al-kibr), the rulers (al-umara') for tyranny (al-jawr), the jurists (al-fuqaha') for jealousy (al-hasad), the merchants (al-tujjar) for fraud/betrayal (al-khiyanah), and the villagers (ahl al-rasatiq) for ignorance (al-jahl).

key_terms.الدَّهَاقِينَ: Landlords or owners of large estates

ai.seo_question: What are the six groups of people and their corresponding sins mentioned in this hadith about divine punishment?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ali (AS) presents a structured theology of social accountability, linking specific societal roles to their characteristic spiritual vulnerabilities. It underscores the Shia emphasis on purifying the elite—whether political, scholarly, or commercial—from the corruption inherent in their positions, such as tribalism for Arabs and jealousy for jurists. This framework serves as a practical guide for self-assessment within the community, warning that status amplifies moral responsibility.
